where: Figure spec at the end of Section 4
problem: The caption says the hub applies local rules and that 'the local path never depends on the cloud', but the block diagram has no edge from the hub to the relay. The only path to the relay lamp runs cloud → relay. A student reading the figure sees local control producing no action, which contradicts Sections 1 and 2.
fix: Add the local path: {'from': 'hub', 'to': 'relay', 'label': 'command (local)', 'style': 'solid'}, and keep the cloud → relay edge labelled 'command (remote)'. Update the aria text to say the hub switches the relay locally and the cloud can also command it.

problem: The claim 'Most of a smart home bill is standby power' is contradicted by the chapter's own worked example, where the always-on hub and cameras are 312 of 762 Wh/day, about 41 %, which is not most. It also stretches the standard meaning of standby power (power drawn while a device is idle or in low-power mode) to cover devices doing useful work 24 h a day.
fix: Write: 'A large share of a smart home bill is always-on power. Bulbs run a few hours, but the hub and the cameras run all day — nearly half the energy in the example below — so they must be counted for 24 h.'

problem: The rule example uses lux ('IF motion = 1 AND lux < 200'), and Section 3's code uses a light level, but no light sensor appears among the sensors listed (PIR, door, temperature). The reader never learns which device produces lux.
fix: Add one line to the sensor list: 'A light sensor (an LDR or photodiode, often read through an ADC) reports illuminance in lux; the hub uses it to decide whether a room is dark enough to need the lamp.'
